tier-1: I Associate * Focuses on foundational design execution, learning design system standards, and delivering UI/UX assets under close mentorship. Provides wireframes, mockups, and prototypes. Collaborates with Engineering and Product to ship defined feature components. Hones craft, actively applies user feedback, and consistently delivers clean, spec-ready designs within scope.
tier-2: II Mid-level * Independently owns the end-to-end user experience for specific product features or initiatives with minimal daily supervision. Distills user research to actionable direction while translating Product goals into design artifacts. Contributes to scaling design systems and works directly with engineers and product leads to ensure seamless implementation, balancing design quality with technical constraints.
Tier-3: III Senior * Operates with high autonomy. Leads complex design initiatives that drive business metrics and resolve key user pain points. Partners closely with Product and technical leads to influence roadmaps. Validates concepts through exploratory research, and maintains craft excellence. Builds team strength by establishing Design team processes, guiding critique sessions, and mentoring junior design peers.
Tier-4: IV Lead * Balances IC work with project coordination, cross-functional collaboration, and peer mentorship as a domain owner. Orchestrates multi-designer workflows across varied product areas, ensuring visual and structural consistency across teams.  Facilitates collaborative design sprints. Serves as a bridge between individual contributors and leadership to articulate product design strategy, set quality bars, and unblock execution hurdles for the team.
Tier-5: V Principal * Operates across multiple product streams to define long term user experience vision and drive large scale initiatives. Untangles highly ambiguous product challenges, pioneers new interaction patterns, and aligns executive priorities with customer-centric product strategy. Elevates the organization's overarching design architecture, influences high level business goals, and sets the technical standards for the design discipline rather than managing daily feature output.

definition: Understanding of design tools, theory, and systems, component architecture, and multi-platform consistency.
tier-1: Executes foundational UI designs using existing design system UI kits and core tool features
tier-2: Proficient with UI component libraries and responsive layout principles; builds polished wireframes and interactive prototypes independently.
Tier-3: Advanced tool proficiency; crafts multi-platform flows, contributes new patterns/components to the design system, and maintains pixel-perfect UI quality.
Tier-4: Expert in design systems architecture; defines complex layout logic, interactive patterns, and sets production-grade tool/asset standards for the team.
Tier-5: Drives cross-platform visual and technical alignment across multiple team domains; identifies and resolves system debt and architectural gaps.

definition: Able to create design artifacts that demonstrate complex logic, motion, and edge-case behavior that integrate into and expand existing systems.
tier-1: Identifies edge cases in basic user flows and builds designs that follow existing system guidelines.
tier-2: Uncovers non-happy-path scenarios, state changes, and error handling; crafts modular design solutions that scale across core features.
Tier-3: Maps complex system dependencies and edge-case logic; creates reusable pattern families that simplify multi-product workflows.
Tier-4: Architect of scalable product frameworks. Anticipates long-term system implications and handles complex multi-touchpoint journeys gracefully.
Tier-5: Standardizes system-level component behavior and interaction patterns across enterprise product ecosystems while mitigating legacy complexity.

definition: Connects design decisions to core business metrics like conversion, retention, churn, and Customer Lifetime Value.
tier-1: Understands basic product goals and key performance metrics relevant to immediate feature work.
tier-2: Articulates how individual design decisions impact product metrics and user goals; uses analytics to validate feature changes.
Tier-3: Defines success metrics alongside Product. Uses quantitative data, research, and testing to iterate and optimize user paths.
Tier-4: Connects strategic design decisions directly to business outcomes. Influences product roadmaps by identifying high-impact design opportunities.
Tier-5: Drives cross-functional metrics across business units. Establishes UX benchmark frameworks that track long-term product health and ROI.

definition: Looks beyond feature execution to help shape product roadmaps, define MVP scopes, and map long-term user journeys.
tier-1: Executes on immediate feature tasks. Understands the direct goal of the assigned project.
tier-2: Contributes to project scoping; defines MVP feature requirements and maps end-to-end user journeys for immediate feature initiatives.
Tier-3: Helps shape team goals and identifies roadmap opportunities by aligning user needs with feature improvements.
Tier-4: Partners with Product and Tech Leads to drive product strategy. Frames long-term vision and balances MVP trade-offs against strategic goals.
Tier-5: Defines multi-quarter strategic product visions across product domains while anticipating industry shifts. Leverages Design voice to gain alignment across internal domains like Product and Technology.

definition: Can speak to cross-functional considerations like technical constraints, feasibility, timelines while advocating for user needs.
tier-1: Collaborates effectively with immediate PM and engineering peers. Asks clarifying questions about technical constraints and timelines.
tier-2: Proactively engages cross-functional partners. Balances technical feasibility with user needs during design discussions.
Tier-3: Facilitates design alignment workshops and manages stakeholder feedback effectively. Advocates for usability standards without stalling engineering velocity.
Tier-4: Mentors junior designers and gides cross-functional alignment across projects. Navigates ambiguous stakeholder trade-offs smoothly, gainig trust and moving development forward.
Tier-5: Leads organization-wide design initiatives. Elevates design culture, influences senior cross-functional leaders, and resolves team-level conflicts.

definition: Uses research and analytics as the foundation of their creative process to ensure all decisions directly serve user needs and business goals.
tier-1: Gathers user feedback through basic usability testing, desk research and competitive analysis. Leverages existing data points to validate individual component designs and refine tactical UI solutions.
tier-2: Plans and conducts qualitative user research sessions to surface core user needs and identify key pain points. Analyzes product usage alongside qualitative findings to inform design decisions and iterate on feature flows.
Tier-3: Evaluates complex behavioral data and exploratory research to identify broader product opportunities and validate product strategy. Establishes clear success metrics with cross functional partners to measure design impact across entire user journeys.
Tier-4: Defines research frameworks across multiple squads to ensure cohesive insights feed into product strategy and feature roadmaps. Champions data informed design practices and connects user insights directly to business metrics for executive stakeholders.
Tier-5: Utilizes advanced research methodologies to evaluate emerging product opportunities and anticipate long term customer behaviors. Translates macro market trends and organizational data assets into high level strategic vision across entire product lines.

tier-1: I Associate * Supports a defined slice of the product under close mentorship. Writes clear tickets, keeps status visible, and ships scoped changes with Engineering and Design. Learns the user, the metrics, and the delivery process. Escalates risks early and delivers reliable, well-communicated work within an established roadmap.
tier-2: II Mid-level * Independently owns the end-to-end outcome for a feature or workstream with minimal daily supervision. Frames the problem, sequences an MVP, and partners with Design and Engineering through launch. Uses research and product data to choose among options, and balances customer value with delivery constraints.
Tier-3: III Senior * Operates with high autonomy on ambiguous, high-impact problems. Sets goals, defines success metrics, and leads discovery through delivery for a product area. Influences the team roadmap, runs effective decision forums, and raises the quality of product thinking across the squad.
Tier-4: IV Lead * Balances hands-on product work with coordination across squads. Orchestrates multi-team initiatives, aligns Design, Engineering, and GTM, and unblocks execution. Mentors other PMs, sets the quality bar for specs and reviews, and translates strategy into a coherent sequence of bets.
Tier-5: V Principal * Operates across product streams to set long-term direction. Untangles highly ambiguous market and organizational problems, aligns executives on customer-centric strategy, and defines the product operating system rather than managing daily feature output.

definition: Judgment for which problems are worth solving and which solutions will work for users and the business.
tier-1: Explains the user and the job to be done for assigned work. Distinguishes symptoms from the underlying problem with guidance.
tier-2: Frames feature problems independently. Chooses among solution options using user evidence and product constraints.
Tier-3: Spots the highest-leverage problem in a messy space. Kills weak ideas early and backs the ones that change user behavior.
Tier-4: Sets product quality bars for a domain. Coaches others on problem framing and reviews specs for outcome, not output.
Tier-5: Defines how the organization identifies valuable problems. Resolves conflicting user, business, and technical narratives into a clear point of view.

definition: Ability to scope, sequence, and ship work with Design and Engineering while managing risk, dependencies, and cadence.
tier-1: Breaks assigned work into tickets, tracks status, and flags blockers. Ships defined scope on the team cadence.
tier-2: Owns a feature through launch. Scopes MVPs, manages dependencies, and keeps stakeholders current without being asked.
Tier-3: Runs complex deliveries across multiple workstreams. Cuts scope to protect outcomes and keeps the team moving through ambiguity.
Tier-4: Orchestrates multi-squad launches. Anticipates delivery risk, builds operating rhythms, and unblocks other PMs and partners.
Tier-5: Designs the delivery system for a product area. Sets standards for planning, launch, and operational excellence across teams.

definition: Connects product decisions to measurable outcomes such as activation, retention, conversion, and revenue.
tier-1: Understands the goals and key metrics for assigned features. Checks results after ship with support.
tier-2: Defines success metrics for a feature and uses dashboards or analyses to iterate after launch.
Tier-3: Sets area-level goals with partners. Instruments journeys, reads leading and lagging indicators, and changes course from evidence.
Tier-4: Ties the roadmap to business outcomes. Builds measurement frameworks others reuse and challenges vanity metrics.
Tier-5: Establishes product health and ROI frameworks across businesses. Uses metrics to set investment levels and retire work.

definition: Looks beyond the next feature to shape roadmaps, define MVPs, and sequence bets against a longer-term product direction.
tier-1: Executes on assigned roadmap items. Understands why the current project exists.
tier-2: Contributes to scoping. Maps the journey for an initiative and names what is in or out of the MVP.
Tier-3: Shapes team goals and surfaces roadmap opportunities by pairing user need with business timing.
Tier-4: Partners with leads to set multi-quarter direction. Makes explicit trade-offs between now, next, and later.
Tier-5: Defines multi-quarter vision across domains, anticipates market shifts, and aligns Product, Design, and Technology on the bet.

definition: Works across Design, Engineering, GTM, and leadership to create clarity, resolve tension, and keep decisions moving.
tier-1: Collaborates with immediate Design and Engineering partners. Asks clarifying questions about constraints and timelines.
tier-2: Proactively engages partners. Brings the right people into the discussion and closes loops without being chased.
Tier-3: Facilitates alignment meetings and handles stakeholder feedback. Holds the user and the outcome without stalling the team.
Tier-4: Mentors PMs and guides cross-functional alignment across projects. Navigates political trade-offs and earns trust.
Tier-5: Leads organization-wide product initiatives. Influences senior leaders, raises the product culture, and resolves team-level conflict.

definition: Uses qualitative research, experiments, and product data to de-risk decisions before and after build.
tier-1: Gathers feedback through support tickets, lightweight interviews, or usability sessions. Uses existing data to sanity-check a solution.
tier-2: Plans discovery for a feature. Runs interviews or tests, pairs findings with usage data, and changes the spec from what is learned.
Tier-3: Runs discovery on ambiguous opportunities. Mixes research methods, sets hypotheses, and validates strategy with evidence.
Tier-4: Defines discovery practices across squads. Makes sure insights reach the roadmap and that teams share what they learn.
Tier-5: Uses advanced research and market signals to anticipate customer behavior. Turns insight into portfolio-level bets.
